en: "Welcome to you, monks! Your renunciation has been well-performed, monks! You have gained a great gain, at some time or other."
Rebirth in a noble realm, the possession of unimpaired faculties, being neither dull-witted nor mute, not being one who cannot speak with his hands,
and the capacity to understand the meaning of teachings that are well-spoken or ill-spoken.

And now, I have arisen in the world as a Teacher— a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a Teacher.

Among gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One, teaches the Dharma which leads to tranquility, leads to final nirvana, leads to full awakening, and has been proclaimed by the Sugata. That is to say: when this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises.
Namely: with ignorance as condition, volitional formations arise, and so on, until there is the arising and the cessation [of the whole mass of suffering].

"Monks, this is extremely difficult to obtain, even very difficult to obtain: that one is born at some time or another in a noble realm, with unimpaired faculties, and that there is both the arising and the cessation [of suffering].
Therefore, monks, seeing it as for their own sake, for the sake of others, and for the sake of both, you should train yourselves in this way."
The Sūtra of Welcome is completed. The end. Samāptam.
